cases.final_diagnosis: Developing equipment problem on CNC-02 — most consistent with bearing or axis-drive wear — causing sustained vibration above the 4.50 mm/s alarm setpoint. This is CNC-02-specific, not line-wide: vibration stayed elevated through tick 940 (max 4.633 mm/s in the 934-940 window, means about 4.38-4.41 mm/s across all post-alarm windows) with recurring alarms at ticks 914, 919, 922, 926 and 928, while CNC-02 power draw held steady near 10.4 kW and every other running machine (CNC-04, CNC-05, CNC-06, CNC-07, CNC-08) ran at roughly 1.7-2.6 mm/s. A transient spike is ruled out by the repeated alarms and the still-high readings at tick 940, and a line-wide or environmental cause is ruled out by the normal readings on the other machines.

CNC-05 shows persistently elevated vibration (~4.0-4.5 mm/s) with isolated threshold crossings at ticks 826 and 828 (4.56 and 4.57 mm/s above the 4.50 mm/s alarm threshold). All other CNC-05 sensors are flat and normal: power was ~12.45 kW at both alarm ticks (well within the 12.2-12.7 kW normal range), load mean 68.96%, temperature mean 147.19 °F, following_error mean 4.96 µm with no spike. CNC-05's vibration is roughly double the other CNC machines (CNC-01 mean 1.00, CNC-02 mean 2.06, CNC-03 mean 1.05, CNC-04 mean 1.80 mm/s). The elevated vibration predates job 9 (ticks 800-816 mean 4.04 mm/s), so it is not job-specific. No mechanical fault is indicated: there is no power draw increase, load increase, temperature rise, or following_error growth at or after the alarm ticks. The most consistent explanations are H2 (vibration sensor calibration drift/bias reading ~2 mm/s high) or H3 (CNC-05's normal operating band with a fixed 4.50 mm/s threshold that is too low for this machine). Neither H2 nor H3 can be confirmed over the other with current data, and neither is addressable by the available repair actions (replace_bearing, reset_setting, replace_servo_drive, repair_hydraulics).

Batch-2 incoming material variation or contamination (H1) best explains the anomaly. All three failed inspections (jobs 11, 13, 15) carry batch_id 2 and failed at ticks 1086, 1222, and 1364 (E4, E5, E18, E19), while every batch-1 job (jobs 1-10) passed inspection: 0/10 rejects for batch 1 versus 3/5 rejects for batch 2 so far (E5). The passed batch-2 jobs (12, 14) do not clear the lot, matching the manual's guidance that a bad lot raises the reject rate without failing every part (E2). No machine or inspection alarm coincides with the failure ticks, and vibration on CNC-01 through CNC-06 is within comparable normal bounds (means roughly 1.7-2.1 mm/s; CNC-05 is idle) (E3, E10-E16, E20), arguing against a CNC fault (H2) or inspection-station drift (H3) as the primary cause. Confidence is about 0.80, below the 0.90 intervene threshold; it would be raised by material certificates/receiving inspection showing batch-2 variation (T1), a batch-3 reject-rate check (T2), and an inspection-calibration check around tick 1000-1085 (T3).

The inspection failures are a material-lot problem, not a machine fault. Jobs 11, 12 and 13 are all batch 2 and all failed inspection (3 of 3, 100% reject rate), while jobs 6-10 are all batch 1 and all passed (5 of 5, 0%). The batch-2 jobs ran over different machine sequences, so no single station explains them, and the manual's batch-based guidance (a clearly higher reject rate in one batch points at the material even when some of its jobs pass) matches this pattern exactly. Sensor trends show no abnormal shift around the failure window: CNC-06 vibration mean 1.861 (ticks 1180-1220) versus 1.62-2.19 earlier, CNC-06 following_error mean 3.719 (ticks 1200-1220) versus 3.69-4.72 earlier, CNC-05 vibration mean 1.825 (ticks 1180-1220) versus 1.4-2.0 earlier, and CNC-02/CNC-03 readings are likewise stable. CNC-01 and CNC-04 sensors were not retrieved, but both stations also processed batch-1 jobs that passed immediately before the batch-2 failures, so a station-specific fault is not supported. None of the four approved repairs (bearing, speed reset, servo drive, hydraulics) addresses incoming material, so no factory change is indicated.

Inspection failures (jobs 1, 2, 4) all occur immediately after CNC-05 processing, but no CNC fault is confirmed. CNC-02 vibration is elevated (means ~1.8-2.4) yet that elevation predates every failure (E18: ticks 60-450), so it is a long-standing baseline, not a new fault (H2b). All five CNCs show comparable recent vibration (E7, E11, E15-E17); CNC-05 vibration is normal (E7). CNC-05 following_error (E19) does not cleanly separate the passed job from the failed jobs: approximate window means are ~3.1 (job 1), ~3.7 (job 2), ~2.7 (job 3, passed), ~2.8 (job 4), and job 3's bucket maximum (4.483, ticks 390-419) even exceeds job 4's (4.15, ticks 480-509). So an intermittent CNC-05 fault (H4) is not supported by the signal data, while a CNC-04 fault (H1) is contradicted by clean CNC-04 vibration (E15). Cause remains isolated to neither a machine nor confirmed: inspection-station or incoming-material variation (H2) is possible but unverified, and no intervention reaches the 0.90 confidence threshold.
